description:
FILED s525r (the runtime review, Fable fork, 2026-10-24) from its per-op probe set; PRE-EXISTING (main ef5df65a).  Not fixed.

REPRO (scratch probes/shift.pl):  print -1 >> 1, " ", -8 >> 1, " ", (1 << 63) >> 63, " ", -1 << 1, " ", -1 >> 63, " ", 2**64 >> 1, "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: 9223372036854775807 9223372036854775804 1 18446744073709551614 1 9223372036854775807
  PCL        : -1 -4 1 -2 -1 9223372036854775808

REFERENCE: pp.c:2164 PP(pp_left_shift) / 2203 pp_right_shift -- outside `use integer` the left operand is read with SvUV_nomg (a negative IV becomes its two's-complement UV; an NV above UV_MAX casts to UV_MAX), the shift is UV_LEFT_SHIFT / UV_RIGHT_SHIFT (S_shift_amount at 2106 handles a negative shift count by reversing direction).  Under `use integer` perl shifts the signed IV -- which is what PCL does ALWAYS.

WHERE IT BELONGS: docs/not-supported.md "Integers are unbounded: PCL has no 64-bit boundary" (USER 2026-09-07, #1513) lists three faces (arithmetic promotion to NV, `use integer` wrap, %u/%d clamping) and #1515 three more (int(), division past 2**53); THIS is a further face -- the UV reinterpretation of a negative shift operand -- not in either table.  Unlike the arithmetic faces it is CHEAP to implement exactly without a 64-bit model: in the shift operators (grep `p-<<` / `p->>` / the shift helper in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), when `use integer` is not in force, map a negative integer operand to (ldb (byte 64 0) n) and clamp a double > 2**64-1 to 2**64-1 before shifting; one minusp test per shift.  Guard: a Pl/t row with the six values above (perl-probed), inverse-verified on the base.

Related: #1040 (a numeric-LOOKING string takes the numeric bitwise op -- the POK-vs-IOK memory question; the review's Q1), #1513, #1515, #3692.
=== DONE (s525u) ===
p-<< / p->> read the LEFT operand as perl's SvUV (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
%pcl-uv-coerce, %p-uv-shift, %p-shift): a negative operand is its 64-bit
two's complement (clamped at IV_MIN, so -Inf and -(2**70) are IV_MIN), NaN 0,
+Inf and >= 2**64 UV_MAX; a left shift is kept to 64 bits; a count >= 64 is 0
either way, a negative count reverses.  `use integer' keeps p-<<-int / p->>-int.
Probes (scratch/s525u/probes/shift.pl, 25 lines): 23 of 25 identical to perl
(base: 10); the two left are `-1 >>= 1' / `-1 <<= 1' OUTSIDE `use integer':
the compound pair keeps the signed shift because the compiler emits the same
macro in and out of the pragma -> #3781.  Positive operands unchanged
(`7 >> 1', `1 << 62', `2**62 << 1').  perl-tests/bop.t: the two rows "neg UV
(sic) left/right shift" pass (485/24 -> 487/22), both left fail-baseline.tsv
by edit.  Guard Pl/t/numify-flag-01.t u01-u08 / p01 / i01-i02 (fail on main).
subject: DIVERGENCE (bit shift, a #1513 face, pre-existing): a NEGATIVE left operand of >> / << is a UV in perl (-1 >> 1 = 9223372036854775807, -1 << 1 = 18446744073709551614, -8 >> 1 = 9223372036854775804) where PCL shifts the signed integer (-1, -2, -4); an NV above UV_MAX saturates to UV_MAX before the shift (2**64 >> 1 = 9223372036854775807, PCL 9223372036854775808)
